A level that includes reward chests finishes generating → At least one reward chest tile is visible along an outer edge of the board.
A character path visits a tile adjacent to an unlooted reward chest → The adjacent reward chest changes from closed to open, and a reward selection panel appears.

A blank card is created adjacent to an unlooted reward chest while the relic that lets empty cards open chests is active → The adjacent reward chest changes from closed to open, and a reward selection panel appears.

A character path visits a tile orthogonally adjacent to two or more unlooted reward chests → At least two adjacent reward chests are open, and a reward selection panel appears with the title text "PICK YOUR REWARDS!".
A character path visits a tile diagonally adjacent to an unlooted reward chest → The diagonal reward chest remains closed and no reward selection panel appears from that tile visit.

A character path visits a tile orthogonally adjacent only to an already looted reward chest while no reward panel is open → The already opened chest remains open, and no reward selection panel appears.
A reward selection opens with one required pick → A reward panel is visible with the title text "PICK YOUR REWARD!" above the reward choices.
A reward selection opens with more than one required pick → A reward panel is visible with the title text "PICK YOUR REWARDS!" above the reward choices.
A reward selection opens while the active reward option count is four → The reward panel displays four separate reward choices.
A reward selection opens on the first level → The reward panel displays card-shaped reward choices rather than relic-icon reward choices.
A reward selection opens on a level after the first and the relic-reward branch is selected → The reward panel displays relic-icon reward choices rather than card-shaped reward choices.

An unhovered reward choice is clicked while a reward selection is available → The reward choice remains in the reward panel and is shown in its hovered highlight state; no reward choice is removed by that click.
A hand card is clicked while a reward selection is available → The reward panel remains visible and the hand card is not shown as the selected card for placement.

A reward is chosen while at least one required reward pick remains afterward → The chosen reward is removed from the reward choices, and the reward panel title displays "PICK N MORE!" with N as the visible remaining pick count.
The final required reward choice begins resolving while the reward panel is open → The reward panel disappears and the reward choices are no longer visible.

A card reward is chosen while a card reward selection is available and the visible hand has an available unlocked slot → The chosen card reward is removed from the reward choices, and that card appears in the player's visible hand area.
A relic reward is chosen while a relic reward selection is available → The chosen relic reward is removed from the reward choices and appears in the player's collected relic display.

A SAINTHOOD relic reward is chosen while a relic reward selection is available → The chosen relic is removed from the reward choices, its icon appears in the collected relic display, and the HUD maximum-life number increases by 2.

A MAGNA CARTA relic reward is chosen while a relic reward selection is available and the draw pile can fill the new hand slot → The chosen relic is removed from the reward choices, its icon appears in the collected relic display, and the hand fills to show one additional card compared with the hand count before the relic was chosen.

A relic reward choice becomes hovered while a reward selection panel is open → A tooltip appears by the relic reward choice showing the relic name and description text with colored gem-name highlights.

The player's remaining life is reduced to zero during active gameplay → A dark horizontal game-over panel is visible over the play area with centered text "SIEGE ENDED!" and a centered "TRY AGAIN?" button.
The game-over screen is visible and the restart button is activated → The game returns to an active play layout showing "LIFE: 5/5", score "0", no collected relic icons, and the first-level board.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款在三维场景中以大炮击毁城堡的 Cannonbolf 游戏：玩家从标题菜单进入瞄准视角，移动鼠标调整带碰撞预测的弹道指引，发射炮弹并在飞行视角中观察普通或高弹力表面的反弹。游戏还需呈现弹药、城堡和关卡 HUD、重置与越界失败、城堡碎裂残骸，以及 BIRDIE、PAR 和最终通关等完整反馈与关卡流转。

requirements.zh: The gameplay view has completed its initial setup in Menu mode → A title screen is visible with the text "CANNONBOLF" near the upper middle of the screen and "CLICK TO START" near the bottom middle of the screen.
The player clicks while the game is in Menu mode → The title-screen text disappears and the view changes to an aiming scene with the cannon visible and an aiming guide line drawn from the cannon.

A valid shot is accepted while the game is in FirstAim mode with ammo remaining → On the first rendered gameplay frame after the shot is accepted, the aiming guide line is gone, a ball is visible in play, and the cannon is visible.

A valid shot is accepted while the game is in LaterAim mode with ammo remaining → On the first rendered gameplay frame after the shot is accepted, the aiming guide line is gone, a ball is visible in play, and the cannon is visible.
The player presses the reset key while the game is in Ball mode → A centered message reading "SORRY, TRY AGAIN!" is displayed over the gameplay view.
The ball falls below the level-failure boundary while the game is in Ball mode → A centered message reading "SORRY, TRY AGAIN!" is displayed over the gameplay view.
The player clicks while the game is in Ball mode with no ammo remaining → A centered message reading "SORRY, TRY AGAIN!" is displayed over the gameplay view.

The win-result display on a non-final level has completed its delay → The win message is no longer displayed. An aiming view is visible with the cannon and aiming guide line, and the level-progress HUD line in the new aiming view shows a numerator one greater than the level-progress HUD line shown before the win message appeared.

The failure-result display has completed its delay → The "SORRY, TRY AGAIN!" message is no longer displayed. An aiming view is visible with the cannon and aiming guide line, and the level-progress HUD line shows the same fraction as the level-progress HUD line shown before the failure message appeared.
The player clicks while the game is in Ball mode with ammo remaining → The moving ball is replaced by an aiming view with an aiming guide line visible from the ball's last play position.

A Ball-mode physics frame advances while the ball is airborne and not colliding with a world surface → Between the preceding rendered frame and the next rendered frame, the ball is visible at a new position along its flight path.

The ball contacts a world surface while moving into that surface in Ball mode → At the contact point, the ball remains outside the surface and its subsequent visible motion changes from moving into the surface to moving away from the surface.
The player moves the mouse to the right while the game is in FirstAim mode → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot horizontally to the right from their immediately preceding orientation.
The player moves the mouse to the left while the game is in FirstAim mode → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot horizontally to the left from their immediately preceding orientation.

The player moves the mouse upward while the game is in FirstAim mode and the vertical aim is not at its upper limit → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot upward from their immediately preceding orientation.

The player moves the mouse downward while the game is in FirstAim mode and the vertical aim is not at its lower limit → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot downward from their immediately preceding orientation.
The player moves the mouse to the right while the game is in LaterAim mode → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot horizontally to the right from their immediately preceding orientation.
The player moves the mouse to the left while the game is in LaterAim mode → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot horizontally to the left from their immediately preceding orientation.

The player moves the mouse upward while the game is in LaterAim mode and the vertical aim is not at its upper limit → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot upward from their immediately preceding orientation.

The player moves the mouse downward while the game is in LaterAim mode and the vertical aim is not at its lower limit → The cannon barrel and the aiming guide line pivot downward from their immediately preceding orientation.
The player moves the mouse to the right while the game is in Ball mode → The camera view pivots horizontally to the right around the visible ball.
The player moves the mouse to the left while the game is in Ball mode → The camera view pivots horizontally to the left around the visible ball.
The player moves the mouse upward while the game is in Ball mode and the camera pitch is not at its upper limit → The camera view tilts upward around the visible ball.
The player moves the mouse downward while the game is in Ball mode and the camera pitch is not at its lower limit → The camera view tilts downward around the visible ball.
The final-level win-result display has completed its delay → The centered message reading "THANKS FOR PLAYING!" remains displayed over the gameplay view.

An unhit castle is processed as hit while at least one other castle remains unhit → The intact castle at that location is no longer drawn, multiple separate debris pieces appear at the castle's former position, and no centered result message is displayed.

The final unhit castle is processed as hit on a non-final level with at least one ammo remaining → The intact castle at that location is no longer drawn, multiple separate debris pieces appear at the castle's former position, and a centered message reading "BIRDIE!" is displayed over the gameplay view.

The final unhit castle is processed as hit on a non-final level with no ammo remaining → The intact castle at that location is no longer drawn, multiple separate debris pieces appear at the castle's former position, and a centered message reading "PAR!" is displayed over the gameplay view.

The final unhit castle is processed as hit on the final level → The intact castle at that location is no longer drawn, multiple separate debris pieces appear at the castle's former position, and a centered message reading "THANKS FOR PLAYING!" is displayed over the gameplay view.

The aiming prediction reaches an unhit castle within the castle hit radius while an aiming guide is being drawn → The aiming guide line terminates at that castle and does not visibly continue past the castle.
The aiming prediction reaches a world surface while an aiming guide is being drawn → The aiming guide line terminates at the surface contact point and does not visibly continue through the surface.

A gameplay UI frame is rendered while the game is in FirstAim mode → Three right-aligned HUD lines are visible near the upper-right of the screen: an ammo number followed by "⚫", a castle-hit fraction followed by "🏰", and a level-progress fraction followed by "⛳". A hint text line is centered along the bottom edge of the screen.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款按周经营街市摊位的像素风模拟游戏：玩家从主菜单进入进货、库存定价、市场售卖和周结算流程，在供应商列表中采购商品、调整各类库存售价，并通过带开合幕帘、行人、摊位和时钟的街景观察销售。游戏还需呈现资金、周数、库存、平均成本、声誉星级、需求和销售明细，支持列表与结算滚动、售罄反馈、资金耗尽结束，以及有余额时推进到下一周。

requirements.zh: The main menu is rendered when no saved game is available → The screen shows the three-line yellow title “𝕄𝕒𝕣𝕜𝕖𝕥”, “𝕊𝕥𝕣𝕖𝕖𝕥”, “𝕋𝕪𝕔𝕠𝕠𝕟” centered near the top, and a vertical menu containing “New Game”, “FullScreen”, “Help”, and “About” with no “Continue” item visible.

The recap confirmation is accepted when the player's money plus recap total is zero → The display changes from the recap flow back to the main menu screen with the “𝕄𝕒𝕣𝕜𝕖𝕥 𝕊𝕥𝕣𝕖𝕖𝕥 𝕋𝕪𝕔𝕠𝕠𝕟” title and its vertical menu.

A downward selection input is accepted on the main menu while the highlighted item is not the bottom item → The main menu remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn on the menu label one row below the label that was highlighted before the input.

An upward selection input is accepted on the main menu while the highlighted item is not the top item → The main menu remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn on the menu label one row above the label that was highlighted before the input.

The stock screen renders a row for a product in the player's stock list → The row shows the product name, a “Stock:” value, an “Avg cost:” dollar value, and a “Reputation:” line containing exactly five reputation symbols.
The recap screen renders a product row with demand information → The row shows the product icon and product name, followed by a “Demand:” line containing exactly ten demand symbols.
The recap screen is rendered while the recap product list contains more than two rows → A white vertical scrollbar is visible along the right side of the recap product list.
The recap screen is rendered when the player's money plus recap total is zero → The recap screen shows the messages “You ran out of money.”, “GAME OVER”, and “Press enter” in the summary area.

A header is rendered for a screen with a supplied total value → The header shows the week and screen title at the upper left, the current money amount at the upper right, and a second upper-right line beginning with “+ ” followed by the total dollar amount.

A header is rendered for a screen with no supplied total value → The header shows the week and screen title at the upper left and the current money amount at the upper right, with no second upper-right line beginning with “+ ”.
The stock screen is rendered while the player has no products in stock → The stock screen shows the header “Stock” and the centered message “Your stock is empty”.

A downward selection input is accepted on the buy screen while the highlighted item is not the bottom item → The buy screen remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn on the supplier row or “next” button one row below the item that was highlighted before the input.

An upward selection input is accepted on the buy screen while the highlighted item is not the top supplier row → The buy screen remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn on the supplier row or “next” button one row above the item that was highlighted before the input.

A purchase confirmation is accepted on a buy screen supplier row whose displayed stock is at least 1 and whose displayed unit price is not greater than the player's displayed money → The same buy screen remains visible; the selected supplier row changes to show “soldout”, and the upper-right header money amount equals the amount shown before confirmation minus the dollar price displayed on that supplier row before confirmation.

A purchase confirmation is attempted on a buy screen supplier row whose displayed stock is 0 → The buy screen remains visible with the supplier row’s displayed stock still at 0 and the header money amount unchanged from before the confirmation.

A purchase confirmation is attempted on a buy screen supplier row whose displayed unit price is greater than the player's displayed money → The buy screen remains visible with the supplier row’s displayed stock value unchanged and the header money amount unchanged from before the confirmation.
A confirmation input is accepted on the buy screen while the “next” item is highlighted → The display changes from the buy screen to the stock screen with the “Stock” header.

A downward selection input is accepted on the stock screen while the highlighted item is not the bottom navigation item → The stock screen remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn one row below the item that was highlighted before the input.

An upward selection input is accepted on the stock screen while the highlighted item is not the top product row → The stock screen remains visible and the visual selection highlight is drawn one row above the item that was highlighted before the input.
A right price-adjustment input is accepted on a stock screen product row → The selected product row’s displayed selling price increases by exactly 1 dollar.

A left price-adjustment input is accepted on a stock screen product row whose displayed selling price is at least 1 dollar → The selected product row’s displayed selling price decreases by exactly 1 dollar.
A left price-adjustment input is accepted on a stock screen product row whose displayed selling price is 0 dollars → The selected product row’s displayed selling price remains shown as 0 dollars.
A confirmation input is accepted on the stock screen bottom navigation item while the back choice is selected → The display changes from the stock screen back to the buy screen.
The delayed forward transition after accepting the stock screen “next” choice completes → The display changes from the stock screen transition to the market scene.
The market screen update occurs after the market timer has ended while the curtain panels are fully closed → The display changes from the market scene to the recap screen with the “Summary” header.

A downward scroll input is accepted on the recap screen while the recap product list is not at its lowest scroll position → The recap product rows shift upward by 20 screen pixels and the scrollbar handle moves downward along the right-side scrollbar.

An upward scroll input is accepted on the recap screen while the recap product list is not at its top scroll position → The recap product rows shift downward by 20 screen pixels and the scrollbar handle moves upward along the right-side scrollbar.
Supplier generation occurs when none of the current supplier prices is affordable with the player's current money → The next buy screen includes a supplier row for “wood”.
The market scene renders exactly one product type with remaining stock → Product icons are drawn in the center box, while the left and right boxes contain no product icons.
The market scene renders exactly two product types with remaining stock → Product icons are drawn in the left and right boxes, while the center box contains no product icons.
The market scene renders exactly three product types with remaining stock → Product icons are drawn in the left, center, and right boxes.
The market scene renders a product whose accumulated sales are at least its starting stock → No icons for that product remain visible in the market boxes.
A left input is accepted on the stock screen while the bottom navigation item is selected → The bottom “back” button is highlighted in white and the “next” button is not highlighted.

A right input is accepted on the stock screen while the bottom navigation item is selected and the stock screen is not empty → The bottom “next” button is highlighted in white and the “back” button is not highlighted.

The stock screen is rendered with at least three product rows while the third product row is selected → The product list is scrolled upward by one row height so the first product row is above the visible stock list area.
The stock screen renders a product row whose reputation value is 0 → The row’s “Reputation:” line contains one full reputation symbol followed by four empty reputation symbols.
The stock screen renders a product row whose reputation value is at least 100 → The row’s “Reputation:” line contains five full reputation symbols and no empty reputation symbols.
The recap screen renders a product row whose normalized demand value is 0 → The row’s “Demand:” line contains ten empty demand symbols and no full demand symbols.
The recap screen renders a product row whose normalized demand value is at least 1 → The row’s “Demand:” line contains ten full demand symbols and no empty demand symbols.
The recap screen renders a product row whose sales expression is 16 characters or fewer → The row’s sales line begins with “Sales: ” followed by the sales expression.

A confirmation input is accepted on the recap screen while the player's money plus recap total is not zero → The display changes from the recap screen to the buy screen for the next week, with the upper-left header showing a week number one higher than the recap screen showed before the confirmation.

The market scene renders its stall background → The scene shows two vertical wooden posts, a horizontal support beam near the top, a red-and-white striped tent cloth, a brick wall band, and three brown display boxes with dark interiors.

The market scene renders its state badges → A white rectangular badge near the upper left shows “Week” followed by the week number, and a white rectangular badge near the upper right shows the displayed money amount followed by “$”.

vlm.zh: A slow-enemies powerup timer is active during gameplay → A translucent blue overlay covers the gameplay view and visible enemies are drawn with a blue-tinted overlay.

replayTrace.zh: The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is disabled, the mouse button is held, and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.
The MENU button is activated from the paused screen and the return-to-menu confirmation is accepted → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while triple shot is active → Three bullet line segments originate from the player ship in a spread pattern.

The gameplay view is first rendered for a newly reset run → The HUD SCORE value reads 000000, the PROGRESS bar has no filled segment extending from its left edge, and a level notification showing 01 is visible in the gameplay view.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay after the triple-shot powerup timer has expired and firing is accepted → Exactly one bullet line segment originates from the player ship.

vlm.zh: The Down movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay and the Up movement input is not held → The player ship's position shifts downward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.

replayTrace.zh: The MENU button is activated from the paused screen and the return-to-menu confirmation is accepted → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.

The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is disabled, the mouse button is held, and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.

replayTrace.zh: A piercing bullet collides with its fourth distinct enemy during active gameplay → Hit particle effects appear at the enemy and the bullet line disappears after the impact.
The PLAY AGAIN button is activated on the game-over screen → The game-over screen is replaced by the active gameplay view for a new run.
The MENU button is activated on the game-over screen → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay after the triple-shot powerup timer has expired and firing is accepted → Exactly one bullet line segment originates from the player ship.
An air boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, yellow air-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
The player's last remaining life is lost → A browser alert dialog appears with the text “You lost.”.
The loss alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.
All waves have been sent and cleared while at least one life remains → A browser alert dialog appears with text beginning “You won! Based on lives and elemental fragments left, your score is:”.
The win alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

vlm.zh: The reclaim control is selected in the open tower upgrade/reclaim menu for an existing tower → The selected tower disappears from its tile, and within 1 second the fragments HUD numeric display shows a value at least 1 above the visible pre-reclaim value, with tolerance 0.

The fifth wave is sent while the sixth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “5 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 13 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The tenth wave is sent while the eleventh wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “10 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 15 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The fifteenth wave is sent while the sixteenth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “15 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 17 fire enemies.
The twentieth wave is sent as the final queued wave → The wave display changes to “20 / 20”, and the Send Wave control is displayed as disabled.

replayTrace.zh: An earth boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, green earth-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
The upgrade button is selected for a tower that is not upgradable → The tower upgrade/reclaim menu remains open, and the upgrade button remains shown as unavailable.
The player's last remaining life is lost → A browser alert dialog appears with the text “You lost.”.
The loss alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.
All waves have been sent and cleared while at least one life remains → A browser alert dialog appears with text beginning “You won! Based on lives and elemental fragments left, your score is:”.
The win alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

vlm.zh: A leftward swipe steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path to the left → The hero moves leftward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
The hero collides with a 404 road-not-found sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → A falling-road segment appears directly after the 404 sign on the road.

replayTrace.zh: A keyboard key release that does not match the next Konami-code key is accepted while the title screen is displayed before the Konami-code sequence is complete → The display changes from the title screen to the gameplay screen.
The gameplay screen is rendered during active play after the road map cache has been built → The gameplay viewport is filled by tiled highway lanes with shoulder tiles along the left and right edges.
A scheduled falling-road spawn becomes due and the new segment does not overlap a 200 road-OK marker → A new falling-road segment appears at the scheduled road position.

The hero overlaps a falling-road segment after that segment has passed the fatal animation frame during active gameplay → The hero is drawn rotated away from its upright orientation during a death animation.

A completed player movement lands on a switch-trigger tile before the step limit is reached → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A right-button tile removal click is accepted on a filled grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to an empty grid cell.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT HAIR COLOR” character customization step → The selected hair-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that hair color.

A crate finishes moving onto a hole tile → The crate and the hole tile at that grid cell are replaced by a filled-hole tile.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable boulder is directly to the right of the player and at least one tile to the right of the boulder can receive it → The boulder moves right along its row until it reaches the last receiving tile before the next blocked tile or border, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A boulder finishes moving with an untriggered gong-trigger tile directly in front of its stopping direction → The gong tile with the same orientation as that gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.
A completed player movement leaves a switch-trigger tile → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A movement command is processed into an untriggered gong-trigger tile during active gameplay → The gong tile with the same orientation as the gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.

The menu background is rendered after its background image is available → A pixel-art background image is repeated horizontally across the visible canvas behind the menu screen.
The game completes initial setup with a valid encoded level parameter in the URL → The display opens directly to gameplay showing the decoded custom level as the active board.

An upward movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination above the player contains a blocking tile that does not perform an action → The player character remains on its current tile and the character sprite faces upward.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable crate is directly to the right of the player and the tile one cell to the right of the crate can receive it → The crate moves one grid cell to the right, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A completed player movement lands on a key tile during active gameplay → The key tile at the player’s destination disappears from the board while the player character remains on that destination tile.
The gameplay UI is rendered during an active built-in level → The UI shows text in the form “LEVEL: ” followed by the current level number, and the reset prompt “R: RESET” is visible.
A tile placement click is accepted on an empty grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to show the currently selected tile using the currently selected orientation.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound enabled → The sound icon changes from the sound-on drawing to the muted sound-off drawing.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound muted → The sound icon changes from the muted sound-off drawing to the sound-on drawing.

replayTrace.zh: The menu overlay reveal sequence has completed → The menu overlay shows the title "Tiny Yurts" and two buttons labeled "Fullscreen" and "Start".

The initial menu screen has completed setup with no stored highscore available → A menu overlay is visible with a button labeled "Start", and the menu text shows the tip "Tip: Left click & drag to connect yurts to" followed by "farms, or delete paths with right click."

The Start button is accepted while the menu playfield is shown in its angled zoomed-in presentation → The menu overlay is no longer visible, and the main gameplay playfield is visible in an unrotated view.
The early active game reaches the score-counter reveal moment → The animal score counters are visible on the HUD.
The first active-game pond spawn chooses the large-pond branch and a valid position is available → A pond occupying a 6 by 4 cell area appears on the playfield.
A newly spawned farm with a predefined starting path reaches its delayed starting-path creation moment → A short visible path segment appears connected to the farm.

The fish-farm spawn opportunity occurs after the fish-farm threshold while no fish farm exists and a large pond is available → A fish farm appears on the pond with a visible stone path segment at the pond edge.
A newly spawned yurt reaches its delayed starting-path creation moment → A short visible path segment appears connected to the yurt.
A newly spawned yurt reaches its resident-arrival moment → Two person icons appear at the yurt.
A yurt rotation to a new facing direction is accepted → The yurt has a short starting path segment on the new facing side, and the previous short starting path segment is absent.
A path deletion request targets a fixed yurt starting path during active gameplay → The yurt's short starting path segment remains visible during the next 0.5 seconds.

The periodic path inventory reward begins while the path inventory displayed count is below 99 → The path tile counter displays "+9" and then returns to a numeric path count during the reward sequence.

The periodic path inventory reward opportunity occurs while the path tile counter displays "99" → The path tile counter continues to display "99" and does not switch to "+9" during the next 3 seconds.
A newly spawned goat farm reaches its first scheduled animal-arrival moment → One goat appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned goat farm reaches its third scheduled animal-arrival moment → A third goat appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned fish farm reaches its first scheduled fish-arrival moment → One fish appears in the fish farm.
A newly spawned fish farm reaches its fifth scheduled fish-arrival moment → A fifth fish appears in the fish farm.
A new goat is added to the playfield → The goat counter area is visible, and the goat counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the goat was added.
A new fish is added to the playfield → The fish counter area is visible, and the fish counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the fish was added.

An ox update occurs while the ox has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the ox's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another ox → The ox's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.

A goat update occurs while the goat has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the goat's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another goat → The goat's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.

A fish update occurs while the fish has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the fish's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another fish → The fish's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.
A farm assigns an available same-type person a route to an undersupplied farm over connected paths → A person icon leaves its yurt and travels along the drawn path toward the farm.
A person at a farm begins a return-home route over connected paths → The person icon leaves the farm and travels along the drawn path toward its yurt.
A person reaches the fish-service tick while at a fish farm → The fish bodies in that fish farm change to the orange fish color one after another.

A person begins leaving a fish farm after the service duration → The person icon leaves the fish farm and travels along the drawn path toward its yurt; the fish bodies in that fish farm change to the shaded water color one after another.
A farm warning is toggled off → The farm warning marker is no longer visible.
An animal warning is toggled on → A warning marker is visible on the animal.
An animal warning is toggled off → The animal warning marker is no longer visible.
An ox farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has two visible adult oxen → The two adult oxen display love indicators, and one baby ox appears at the farm.
A goat farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has two visible adult goats → The two adult goats display love indicators, and one baby goat appears at the farm.
An ox farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has three visible adult oxen and fewer than five total visible oxen → The three adult oxen display love indicators, and two baby oxen appear at the farm.
A fish farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has fewer than nine visible fish → Four additional fish appear in the fish farm.

An ox farm upgrade is rejected because the farm already has at least five visible oxen → The farm's visible ox count remains at its pre-upgrade count and no love indicators appear at that farm during the next 9 seconds.
A goat farm upgrade is rejected while the farm has six visible goats → The farm's visible goat count remains six and no love indicators appear at that farm during the next 9 seconds.
A fish farm upgrade is rejected because the farm already has at least nine visible fish → The farm's visible fish count remains at its pre-upgrade count during the next 11 seconds.
A baby ox becomes an adult during active gameplay → The ox changes from baby rendering to adult rendering, and the ox horns are visible.
A baby fish reaches adulthood during active gameplay → The fish changes from baby rendering to adult rendering.

The terminal game-over camera transition begins for the lost farm → The playfield is rotated and zoomed toward the lost farm, and the animal counters, clock, path-tile indicator, and pause control are hidden.

The game-over overlay content reveal sequence completes → The overlay shows the header text "Game Over", the sentence "Too few people could tend to this farm in time.", and a button labeled "Overlay On/Off".

The game-over screen is shown with yurt, ox, goat, and fish counts available → The game-over overlay includes a numeric text label ending with "settlers", and the number after "Score:" equals the displayed settlers number plus the displayed ox, goat, and fish counts.
The pause control is accepted during active gameplay after pausing is enabled → The pause control changes from a pause-bars symbol to a play symbol while the gameplay playfield remains visible.
The pause control is accepted while gameplay is paused → The pause control changes to a two-vertical-bars pause symbol while the gameplay playfield remains visible.
The grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the standard grid lock is off → The standard grid overlay is visible, and the standard grid button shows a grid/hash icon.
The grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the standard grid lock is on → The standard grid overlay is hidden, and the standard grid button shows an A-shaped automatic-mode icon.
A right-click path deletion is accepted on an existing path during active gameplay → The selected visible path is removed from the playfield.
A left-click path deletion is accepted on an existing path while the red delete grid lock is on → The selected visible path is removed from the playfield.
